findings.title: Mutation hooks attribute every pool write to pale:RS
findings.detail: beginPoolFlowMutation receives only state, so an active pale:RS observer records writes performed for every other pool in the producer loops. Those rows carry the unrelated positive credit/debit while their before/after snapshots remain pale:RS. A real two-pool decay control emitted two rows per turn and the reader rejected the first unrelated row with debit arithmetic mismatch. The one-pool producer fixtures cannot expose this.

findings.title: Enabled observation can change property access and exception order
findings.detail: selectedPool and observePool property reads occur outside any diagnostic containment. In the targeted control, OFF execution mutated the earlier aaa:RS pool from 100 to 98 before the original pale getter exception, while ON threw from beforePhase before the phase was recorded or the earlier mutation occurred (aaa:RS stayed 100). This violates the authorized lazy/caught ON-only read and original exception-order requirement.

findings.title: Reader can declare an incomplete or operand-poisoned envelope valid
findings.detail: The reader requires two successful terminal groups and local phase pairing but no fixed phase inventory, required writer/branch coverage, or positive mutation count. Entire unattempted phase or writer blocks therefore leave no sequence gap and can still qualify. It only checks available delta against credit/returned/debit; it does not bind available_before/available_after operands to snapshots, validate WIA wounded conservation, direct credit composition, displaced contribution arithmetic, decay formula, or zero/skipped semantics. The fixture covers a single decay mutation per turn and does not exercise these false-completeness cases.
findings.evidence: source inspection of the pinned reader and producer fixture
